newsitem.title: USA: Ford chairman reiterates cost cutting goals.
newsitem.headline: Ford chairman reiterates cost cutting goals.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Chairman Alex Trotman on Thursday reiterated Ford's goals to cut costs in 1997 below 1996 levels and reduce car development time to 24 months.
In Ford's annual report, mailed to shareholders Thursday, Trotman said Ford's materials costs in 1996 were held virtually even with the prior year for the first time in the company's history.

"We're projecting that our total costs in 1997 at constant sales volumes will be down from the previous year for the first time in our history -- despite inflation, added product content and increased regulatory costs," Trotman said.

Trotman also said that computer-simulated design and testing will cut the time needed to develop new products will drop from 33 months now to 24 months months in the future -- a 27 percent improvement.
Ford's five-year global product development plan adds more new vehicles with higher quality at a faster rate, Trotman noted, reiterating that it reduces capital spending by more than $11 billion.

Ford's product development has been unified into a single global plan, allowing the number of basic vehicle platforms to drop by 50 percent. At the same time, the number of model variations by platform will increase by 45 percent, and the number of common parts will grow 50 percent.
"The full benefits of this change won't be realized until the end of the decade, but substantial progress already has been made," Trotman said.
Ford also is working with its 15,000 dealers worldwide to create a standard service process that provides high quality, high value repairs and convenient, courteous customer handling.
